title: Will AI Replace Developers It's Already Starting
description:
Are developers who use AI really pulling ahead in 2026? The skill gap between engineers who adopt AI tools and those who resist is widening fast. 

Even highly talented developers with 20+ years of experience are falling behind if they refuse to adapt — while the ones who lean in are shipping more, earning more, and landing bigger opportunities than ever. 

Here's why AI adoption is becoming the dividing line in software engineering careers.

#techwithtim #ai #softwareengineering #programming

top_comments.author: @DrCognitive
top_comments.text:
Well, I've been with you a long time Tim. You probably remember (actually you probably don't) that I wrote you one time about how I was entering a software development degree program in roughly 2022 and how I was excited and I didn't think AI would have that much of an impact because back then AI kind of sucked at coding. It could maybe do like a halfway decent function, but to produce workable code seemed very far off. Boy was I wrong. I never imagined it would advance as fast as it has been. Even after graduating and having worked on learning coding for years before starting school for it, I noticed that with projects that would take me weeks to months to code AI could do just as decent of a job these days in a matter of seconds to minutes. I do think that there will be a day we're the only coding jobs available will be very advanced AI development positions, but we're moving into the era (I believe) where we are going to have software on demand. Similar to Star Trek, will be able to say "AI, create me this kind of program" and it will give us a completely workable, flushed out, bug-free solution that we can use immediately. At the rate things are going, we're going to see that start to show up probably within the next 2 to 5 years for simple multi-layer programs, another 10 years out and you'll be able to generate full and robust programs on the fly. I can already do a pretty decent job of simple web apps.

I think anyone going into software development should really take a long hard look at their prospects down the road. They will be limited, with fierce competition, and an already seasoned market of unemployed developers with tons of experience.

On the flip side, I think AI is probably going to destroy a lot of careers. I can easily see my current career as a clinical psychologist being replaced. Hell, even now when I'm really stuck with a patient or a case, I just tell AI "You're an expert psychologist in the field of whatever disorder. Here are the details of this patient. What are some actionable and workable interventions I can use with this patient." It can often give me things that I haven't thought of and I'm somewhat of an expert in my field with over 18 years of experience with a particular population. 

In fact I think most thinking jobs are going to be replaced with AI in the near future. Shortly after that will be labor jobs as AI and robotics continue to marry up together. 

It's going to be a very interesting world in about 10 years.
